content:
LAREDO — Jose David "JD" Gonzalez is asking voters to make him mayor on November 3, and his pitch is his résumé: a licensed customs broker since 1994, founder of his own brokerage, and since 2022 the president and chairman of the National Customs Brokers and Forwarders Association of America. His campaign's 30th-day-before-election finance report — filed with the City Secretary and posted on the City of Laredo's campaign finance reports page under the October 5, 2026 deadline — is a public record, and it answers a question every voter is entitled to ask: who is paying for this campaign?

What the cover sheet shows

On its Form C/OH cover sheet — which prints the reporting period as August 3 through September 23, 2026 — the Gonzalez campaign reports total political contributions of $0, total political expenditures of $78,174.39, and outstanding loans of $104,100, with $25,925.61 in contributions maintained at the end of the period. His campaign treasurer is Sonia Villarreal. Every dollar in this filing traces back to one man.

The names on the filing — there are none

Schedule A1, the schedule where Texas candidates list the people and organizations who gave them money, is empty. It contains no entries at all: no individuals, no companies, no political action committees — no one from Laredo and no one from anywhere else. The report lists no in-kind contributions either. None of it would be illegal either way — Texas sets no contribution limits in local races, and every dollar must be disclosed, as the law requires. Disclosure exists so voters can judge for themselves whose support a candidate carries into office. In this filing, the answer is that Gonzalez carries no one's support but his own.

The trade question

Gonzalez is not a typical first-time candidate. For more than thirty years he has worked in the industry that moves billions of dollars of cargo across Laredo's bridges — and in June 2026, four months before this election, he sold his firm, Jose D. Gonzalez, CHB, to Imperative Logistics of Portland, Oregon, becoming its Vice President of National Accounts. As mayor of the nation's busiest inland port, he would vote on bridge tolls, port development, and trade infrastructure — decisions that directly affect his industry and his employer. That is why the donor list mattered here, and why its emptiness is the story: contributions from customs brokers, freight forwarders, logistics firms, and trade interests total zero, and contributions connected to Imperative Logistics are zero — he reported no money from his employer, from his industry, or from anyone at all. Whatever questions his job raises for a future Mayor Gonzalez, nobody is financing him.

His own money

The money is all his. Schedule E lists three loans to the campaign, every one of them from Gonzalez himself — each marked as personal funds deposited in the campaign's political account, none from a bank, none with collateral, and no interest or maturity date printed: $35,000 on August 3, 2026; another $35,000 on August 17, 2026; and $34,100 on September 11, 2026 — $104,100 in all. (The schedule prints his occupation as "Custom Broker" and his address as 2814 Mellville Loop; the report's cover sheet and Schedule F4 print 2815 Mellville Loop. Webb Watch reports the discrepancy as it appears in the filing.) The arithmetic closes exactly: he lent himself $104,100, spent $78,174.39, and had $25,925.61 left at the end of the period. Schedule F4 also shows a single $1,432.00 American Express item, payable to Jose David "JD" Gonzalez himself. A candidate who has just sold his company is positioned to self-fund, and there is nothing improper about it — self-funding is lawful, and here it is disclosed right on Schedule E, as the law requires. But voters are entitled to know whether they are being asked to elect a campaign, or to ratify one man writing his own check.

The rest of the field, for scale

In the same reporting window, Council Member Alyssa Cigarroa reported $374,500 in contributions. Mayor Victor Treviño reported $2,000 from a single donor, alongside a $200,000 loan from himself. Poncho Casso reported $4,000 from two donors. And Jorge A. Garza, the fifth name on the mayoral ballot, filed no 30th-day report at all. Gonzalez is the only candidate in this race whose filing shows zero dollars from another human being.

The bottom line

A campaign finance report is not an accusation. It is a list of names and numbers that the law makes public precisely so voters can weigh them. Gonzalez's filing — like the filings of Mayor Victor Treviño, Alfonso "Poncho" Casso, and Council Member Alyssa Cigarroa in the same race — shows whose money stands behind the man asking to run a port city. In his case there is no coalition and no crowd of interests: the money is $104,100 of his own, lent to himself. Whether that money is independence, or a campaign of one, is a judgment the report leaves, properly, to the voters of Laredo.

Sources: City of Laredo, Campaign Finance Reports (City Secretary's Office) — https://www.cityoflaredo.com/departments/city-secretary-s-office/campaign-finance-reports ; JD (Jose David) Gonzalez, 30th-day-before-election report, period printed on cover 08-03-26 thru 09-23-26 (posted Oct. 5, 2026) — https://www.cityoflaredo.com/home/showpublisheddocument/24703/639267974366570000 ; JD Gonzalez for Mayor — https://jdformayor.com/ ; Webb Watch 956, "The Broker Running for Mayor: JD Gonzalez's Trade Record, the Business He Just Sold, and the Data Center Question," Oct. 18, 2026 — https://webbwatch956.wordpress.com/2026/10/18/the-broker-running-for-mayor-jd-gonzalezs-trade-record-the-business-he-just-sold-and-the-data-center-question/

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: Jose David "JD" Gonzalez is running for mayor on three decades in Laredo's customs and trade business. His campaign finance report — a public record filed with the City Secretary — answers the question of who is paying for that run with a single name: his own. Gonzalez reported $0 in contributions and financed the entire campaign with $104,100 in loans from himself.
title: Follow the Money: Who Is Financing JD Gonzalez's Run for Mayor?
